entries.value: The Phase 2 trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2023, showed retatrutide achieved up to 24.2% body weight reduction at 48 weeks at the highest dose — exceeding all previous results from any single pharmacological agent.\n\nThe compound was generally well-tolerated, with nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting as the most common adverse events (consistent with GLP-1-class effects). Phase 3 TRIUMPH results have since been published; see the TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 subsections. Publication is not FDA approval, and those figures are not a dose.

TRIUMPH-2 (NCT05929079) was a registrational Phase 3 trial: 1,152 adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥27 kg/m² were randomized to once-weekly retatrutide trial arms (4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks (EASD 2026 presentation; simultaneous Lancet publication, 29 Sep 2026). Figures below describe what was reported in that study — not how anyone should use research materials sold as RUO.

Efficacy estimand (Lilly press release, 29 Sep 2026) — models remaining on assigned intervention without prohibited weight-management treatments:

• 4 mg: mean weight change −12.7% (−29.8 lbs); A1C −1.4
• 9 mg: mean weight change −19.1% (−45.4 lbs); A1C −1.6
• 12 mg: mean weight change −20.8% (−49.6 lbs); A1C −1.5
• Placebo: mean weight change −4.0% (−9.3 lbs); A1C −0.2

Baseline averages cited by Lilly: weight ~106.4 kg, BMI ~38.2 kg/m², A1C ~7.7%. At 12 mg, Lilly reported 52.0% of participants achieving ≥20% weight reduction and 34.9% achieving ≥25% (efficacy estimand); 59.5% no longer met BMI criteria for obesity. Among participants with baseline BMI ≥35, mean loss at 12 mg was reported as 23.4% (60.8 lbs). Up to 40.0% reached A1C <5.7% (not family-wise type I error controlled per Lilly footnote).

Treatment-regimen estimand (Lancet abstract Findings): mean percent weight change −11.9% (4 mg), −16.8% (9 mg), and −18.8% (12 mg) versus −5.1% placebo (estimated treatment differences vs placebo −6.9%, −11.8%, −13.8%; p<0.0001 for all). Prefer stating which estimand you quote; do not mix them in one sentence without labeling.

Safety (Lilly): most common AEs vs placebo included diarrhea (27.4% / 33.5% / 33.6% vs 13.2%), nausea (13.7% / 20.8% / 28.0% vs 8.0%), constipation (14.0% / 16.2% / 16.8% vs 9.4%), decreased appetite (5.8% / 12.3% / 17.1% vs 4.5%), vomiting (5.5% / 10.2% / 15.7% vs 4.2%). Dysesthesia 4.5% / 5.6% / 7.3% vs 0.7%. Discontinuations due to AEs: 3.8% / 11.6% / 7.7% vs 4.9% placebo. Highest-dose CV risk-factor changes reported by Lilly included average reductions of 39.5% triglycerides, 19.6% non-HDL cholesterol, 10.8 mmHg systolic BP, 6.7 in (16.9 cm) waist circumference, and 58.3% hsCRP — risk factors, not CV outcomes from this trial.

human_use_subsections.title: TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3 (NEJM, 29 Sep 2026) — different trial from TRIUMPH-2

entries.value: TRIUMPH-1 (NCT05929066) is not TRIUMPH-2. Jastreboff and colleagues, for the TRIUMPH-1 Investigators, reported it in The New England Journal of Medicine (29 Sep 2026; DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2604169; PMID 42814954): adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, randomized to once-weekly retatrutide 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg or placebo for 80 weeks (2,339 participants). The abstract states that, for weight-related endpoints, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand. Under that analysis, mean percent change in body weight was −17.6% (4 mg), −23.7% (9 mg), and −25.0% (12 mg) versus −3.9% with placebo. Those abstract figures are the treatment-regimen result. They are not a treatment recommendation and not a head-to-head comparison with semaglutide, tirzepatide, or eloralintide. The same paper’s abstract does not print −28.3%. Lilly Medical’s table of TRIUMPH-1 outcomes, which cites that NEJM article, lists a separate efficacy estimand: percent change in body weight at 80 weeks was −19.0% (4 mg), −25.9% (9 mg), and −28.3% (12 mg) versus −2.2% with placebo. −28.3% is not the abstract primary weight result. TRIUMPH-2 remains the separate type 2 diabetes plus obesity or overweight trial; its published figures are not restated here and are not a ranking against TRIUMPH-1. PeptideMap is a research-use (RUO) comparison publisher, not a clinic or pharmacy. This is not medical advice and not a dose.

human_use_subsections.title: TRIUMPH-3 topline (Lilly, 23 Jul 2026) — not a peer-reviewed cardiovascular-outcomes paper

entries.value: No. TRIUMPH-3 (NCT05882045) is not sourced from a peer-reviewed NEJM or Lancet cardiovascular-outcomes paper. Eli Lilly’s 23 July 2026 topline is the source. The trial enrolled adults with severe obesity (BMI ≥35 kg/m²) and established cardiovascular disease, with or without type 2 diabetes (1,949 participants; 9 mg, 12 mg, or placebo; 80 weeks). Under the efficacy estimand in that release, mean percent weight change at 80 weeks was −21.6% (9 mg) and −22.6% (12 mg) versus −3.2% with placebo. That is not the TRIUMPH-1 or TRIUMPH-2 result, and a treatment-regimen weight figure for TRIUMPH-3 was not in the release. The same release reported pre-specified in-study analyses of time to first event for pooled 9 mg and 12 mg versus placebo. MACE-5 was 44 events versus 52 (hazard ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.22). MACE-3 was 27 events versus 23 (hazard ratio 1.12, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.96). Both intervals include 1. The release does not establish a reduction in cardiovascular events. It says these events occurred less frequently than anticipated in both the retatrutide and placebo arms. Urinary tract infection in that topline was 6.1% (9 mg) and 7.0% (12 mg) versus 5.3% with placebo in TRIUMPH-3. This is not medical advice and not a dose.
The TRIUMPH Phase 3 program evaluates retatrutide across related obesity and complication settings. Names below are literacy labels only. Prefer the estimand label printed in the source you cite.

TRIUMPH-1 (NCT05929066) — adults with obesity without diabetes; NEJM 29 Sep 2026 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2604169; PMID 42814954). Abstract weight result uses a treatment-regimen (ITT) estimand: mean percent body-weight change −17.6% (4 mg), −23.7% (9 mg), −25.0% (12 mg) versus −3.9% placebo. A separate efficacy-estimand row of −28.3% at 12 mg (vs −2.2% placebo) appears on Lilly Medical’s TRIUMPH-1 outcomes table citing that paper — keep −25.0% and −28.3% labeled separately; do not present −28.3% as the abstract’s treatment-regimen primary weight line.

TRIUMPH-2 (NCT05929079) — adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight; EASD / Lancet 29 Sep 2026 (DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01861-1). Do not rewrite live figures. Locked efficacy estimand includes up to −20.8% mean weight change at 12 mg vs −4.0% placebo; locked treatment-regimen includes −18.8% at 12 mg vs −5.1% placebo.

TRIUMPH-3 (NCT05882045) — adults with severe obesity (BMI ≥35) and established cardiovascular disease, with or without T2D; Lilly topline 23 Jul 2026 (not treated here as a peer-reviewed cardiovascular-outcomes paper). Efficacy-estimand mean weight change −21.6% (9 mg) and −22.6% (12 mg) versus −3.2% placebo. Pre-specified in-study MACE-5 HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.55–1.22) and MACE-3 HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.64–1.96); intervals include 1 — the release does not establish cardiovascular-event reduction.

Label topline versus peer-reviewed whenever you quote. July 2026 PR Newswire is topline for TRIUMPH-2/3 efficacy-estimand headlines; September 2026 Lancet is peer-reviewed for TRIUMPH-2 treatment-regimen Findings; September 2026 NEJM is peer-reviewed for TRIUMPH-1 treatment-regimen weight means.

human_use_subsections.title: Obstructive sleep apnea trials (NEJM, 21 Oct 2026) — developer-affiliated (Lilly-funded)

entries.value: On 21 October 2026, The New England Journal of Medicine published the TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA results (full title under References) by Grunstein RR, Somers VK, Azarbarzin A, Malhotra A, Sands SA, Lucey BP, Allen SE, Giblin K, Falcon BL, Park SY, Lou J and Krueger K, for the TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA Investigators (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2611477; PMID 42904878). Developer-affiliated: the abstract states the work was funded by Eli Lilly, the company developing retatrutide.

Design (from the abstract): two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within the larger TRIUMPH-1 (NCT05929066) and TRIUMPH-2 (NCT05929079) basket trials. They enrolled adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and a body-mass index of at least 27, without type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-1-OSA, 243 randomized) or with type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2-OSA, 448 randomized). Participants were assigned to one of three retatrutide dose arms or placebo. Baseline mean apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, and baseline mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg.

Primary end point: change in AHI (the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks in the middle and highest dose arms, analyzed with a hybrid-treatment estimand. Mean AHI changes at 80 weeks in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were −22.9 (lowest dose arm), −34.3 (middle) and −31.7 (highest) events per hour versus −9.9 with placebo (differences vs placebo −13.0 [95% CI −23.0 to −3.0], −24.4 [95% CI −34.1 to −14.7] and −21.9 [95% CI −32.2 to −11.5]). In TRIUMPH-2-OSA they were −19.2, −24.7 and −25.4 versus −10.3 with placebo (differences −8.9 [95% CI −15.9 to −2.0], −14.4 [95% CI −21.6 to −7.2] and −15.1 [95% CI −22.5 to −7.7]).

Intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand, differences from placebo in the same arm order: TRIUMPH-1-OSA −13.2 (95% CI −22.6 to −3.9), −24.7 (95% CI −34.1 to −15.3) and −22.5 (95% CI −31.9 to −13.1); TRIUMPH-2-OSA −8.8 (95% CI −15.8 to −1.7), −13.9 (95% CI −21.3 to −6.6) and −15.0 (95% CI −22.5 to −7.4). Label which estimand you quote.

Key secondary end point (treatment-regimen estimand): mean percent change in body weight across the retatrutide arms was −12.5% to −22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and −12.1% to −18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus −4.8% and −5.6% with placebo.

Safety, as summarized in the abstract: the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. The abstract concludes that retatrutide produced significantly greater decreases in AHI than placebo in these trial populations.

Literacy note: these are results from supervised clinical trials in a defined population. Retatrutide is investigational and not approved for obstructive sleep apnea or any other indication. The results do not describe products sold online as retatrutide and are not guidance for use.

TRIUMPH-2 compared retatrutide with placebo, not with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Do not present TRIUMPH-2 percentages as a three-way ranking. Mechanistically, retatrutide adds glucagon receptor agonism to GIP/GLP-1 activity, whereas semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist and tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist — different trials, populations, and endpoints. A dedicated Phase 3 comparison versus tirzepatide (TRIUMPH-5, NCT06662383) is registered separately; do not invent results. Older Phase 2 obesity data (e.g., Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023) remain useful background for non-diabetes obesity cohorts but are not interchangeable with TRIUMPH-2’s diabetes population.

human_use_subsections.title: Reported safety signals outside clinical trials (as of 16 October 2026)

entries.value: This section summarizes reports about products sold under the name retatrutide outside Lilly's clinical trials. It is separate from the TRIUMPH clinical-trial results and does not change them. None of the reports below establishes that retatrutide caused any event. In most cases, the identity, content, and purity of the product involved are unknown. Products sold online under this name are not Lilly trial supply.

FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) death reports, as reported by CBS News. On 13 October 2026, CBS News reported that FDA had received two reports of deaths after people took products claiming to be retatrutide. CBS said it reviewed redacted FAERS reports obtained under the Freedom of Information Act. According to CBS, the first report (July 2026) described a 41-year-old woman who had cardiac arrest; the report listed retatrutide as a "suspect product" obtained "from an unreliable source." The second report (September 2026) described a 49-year-old patient who had severe dehydration, malnutrition, and cardiac arrest after buying the product from an online peptide vendor. CBS reported that it could not independently verify the reports, that FDA declined to say whether it had verified them, and that neither death was connected to a clinical trial. CBS also reported Lilly's statement that the reports "make clear the two individuals were taking black-market retatrutide." PeptideMap has not seen these reports. The public openFDA FAERS data (last updated 30 July 2026) listed 44 reports in which retatrutide appears as a drug name and no report coded as a death. That dataset predates the September report and may not yet include the July report.

Poison center exposures, as reported by CBS News. CBS reported that America's Poison Centers logged 862 retatrutide exposures in the three months ending in September 2026, 460 in the three months before that, and 249 in the first three months of 2026. America's Poison Centers began tracking retatrutide in late 2025. CBS noted that rising counts are common for a newly monitored drug. An exposure call is not a confirmed adverse effect. PeptideMap has not checked these figures against a public America's Poison Centers or NPDS release.

Limits of FAERS. FAERS is a spontaneous reporting system. Reports are not verified by FDA, can be incomplete or duplicated, and do not show that a product caused an event. For grey-market or "research use" products, the substance actually taken is usually unknown. Report counts cannot be used to estimate how often an event happens.

Social-media pharmacovigilance study (JAMA Network Open, 14 October 2026). Sehgal NKR, Tronieri JS, Rader B, Ungar L, and Guntuku SC published "Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide" in JAMA Network Open (doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929). The study was a cross-sectional analysis of 148,640 retatrutide-related Reddit posts and comments. These came from 38,936 users across 27 communities, posted between May 2021 and December 2025. Large language models classified self-reported use and mapped the symptoms users attributed to retatrutide to MedDRA Preferred Terms, and the authors manually validated 100 posts. The models identified 13,589 users reporting current use. Of these, 7,823 had at least one mapped term after prespecified weight-loss and appetite-suppression terms were excluded. Among those 7,823 users, the most frequent terms were increased appetite (17.1%), fatigue (15.2%), increased energy (12.4%), nausea (11.6%), food craving (7.3%), insomnia (6.1%), and heart rate increased (4.8%). The authors note that gastrointestinal symptoms were common but not dominant, which differs from phase 2 trial findings.

Limits the authors themselves state: the findings are hypothesis-generating. Product identity, purity, dose, route, duration, concomitant medications, and medical history cannot be verified. Reddit users may not represent all users, and adverse events may be preferentially reported. The analysis cannot assess incidence, causality, dose-response, or comparative safety. The reported events may also reflect reconstitution practices, and natural language processing and MedDRA mapping may miss or misclassify symptoms. The reports may reflect product variability, peptide stacking, user characteristics, or misattribution. The study's comparison with semaglutide and tirzepatide was descriptive only, with unmatched samples and no statistical tests.
These reports describe unregulated products and cannot be compared directly with the controlled TRIUMPH trial safety data.
